items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: actually took a few lessons with Harris . . .

ctx.x: I think everybody, again, that I listen to has probably been an influence. On the classical side, probably Bartok more than any other person, even though I draw very liberally on other sources, too. But Bartok is the main influence on the classical side. On the jazz side, it really does run the gamut. Of course, Ellington is ubiquitous. You cannot escape him. George Russell [is] a big, big influence, J. J., Gil Evans. I’m probably missing a lot of the players. But virtually everybody that I’ve come into contact…
Tom Beversdorf, and actually took a few lessons with Harris . . .
